title: A SEVEN-LAYER MODEL FOR STANDARDISING AI FAIRNESS ASSESSMENT
benchmark_measurement: The paper proposes a conceptual framework (a seven-layer model) for standardising AI fairness assessment, not a specific benchmark. Within this framework, it identifies 'religion' as an example of a common protected attribute that should be assessed for bias.
findings: The paper does not present empirical findings related to religion. It conceptually identifies religion as a common protected attribute, alongside gender, race, and caste, that is associated with social bias and should be meticulously considered during the pre-processing and feature engineering stage (Layer 3) of AI system development to ensure fairness.
references: Batya Friedman and Helen Nissenbaum. Bias in computer systems. In Computer Ethics, pages 215–232. Routledge, 2017.
